d1.purpose: Show order line items with their product variants, quantities, charges, warehouse locations, and tracking identifiers.
tasks: Find a line by ID, SKU, variant, warehouse, or tracking identifier.
Compare quantities, prices, taxes, and totals across lines.
Read across a line to connect the product and charges with its fulfillment details.
relations: SKU, color, and size jointly identify the product variant.
Quantity, price, tax, and total describe the line's financial information.
Warehouse and tracking identify the fulfillment location and shipment; the dash indicates no tracking value is shown.
roles: The header names each field; each body row is one line item.
ID is a compact locator, while SKU and tracking are longer identifiers.
The numeric columns support comparison; warehouse and tracking support fulfillment lookup.
keep_whole: Short headers, colors, sizes, quantities, and monetary values.
Tracking identifiers should remain continuous whenever space permits.
SKU and warehouse codes are easiest to scan and copy when kept on one line.
may_wrap: SKU and warehouse codes can wrap at hyphens when horizontal space is constrained.
In the viewport-fitting design, the Warehouse header and tracking identifiers must break within their text.
same_scale: Give the short quantity and monetary columns compact widths suited to their contents.
Give the longer identifier and location columns more space according to their actual lengths.
d1.h_vs_v: The table has only three data rows, so wrapping can save horizontal space at a modest vertical cost. Scrolling preserves identifiers and improves cross-row scanning, but fulfillment details may initially lie outside the viewport.

d2.purpose: Show order line items with their quantities, charges, fulfillment locations and shipment identifiers.
tasks: Identify an item by ID, SKU, color and size.
Compare quantities, prices, taxes and totals across items.
Find the warehouse and tracking identifier for a line item.
relations: SKU, color and size describe the same item.
Quantity, price, tax and total form a financial group.
Warehouse and tracking identify fulfillment and shipment details.
roles: The header labels ten fields; each body row represents one item.
ID is a compact locator; SKU and tracking are identifiers.
The monetary and quantity columns support comparison; warehouse provides a location.
keep_whole: Prices, quantities, totals, sizes and colors.
Tracking identifiers and SKU segments whenever space permits.
may_wrap: SKU and warehouse values at meaningful hyphen boundaries.
Tracking identifiers only when a viewport-fitting design requires it.
same_scale: Keep the compact quantity and monetary columns visually comparable while allowing totals enough room.
Give the longer identifier and location columns more space than short attributes.
d2.h_vs_v: A wider table preserves identifiers and compact rows but requires horizontal scrolling to reach shipment details. A fitting table exposes all fields at once, at the cost of taller rows and split identifiers.

d3.purpose: A compact order-line table linking product variants and charges to warehouse and shipment information.
tasks: Find an item by ID or SKU and identify its color and size.
Compare quantities, prices, taxes, and totals across rows.
Locate the warehouse and tracking identifier for a line.
relations: Each row describes one item and its associated financial and fulfillment details.
Color and size qualify the SKU; quantity, price, tax, and total belong together.
Warehouse and tracking identify fulfillment information for the same row.
roles: The header row names ten fields; no column is declared as a row header.
ID and SKU identify lines and products; the remaining columns describe variants, amounts, and fulfillment.
keep_whole: Tracking identifiers should remain intact for reliable lookup and copying.
Numeric amounts, quantities, sizes, and color names should remain whole.
SKU and warehouse identifiers are easiest to recognize when kept on one line.
may_wrap: If space requires it, SKU and warehouse identifiers can wrap at existing hyphens, though this slows scanning.
The fitting layout must also split some unbreakable text, including tracking identifiers.
same_scale: Keep the short variant and numeric columns compact and broadly comparable in scale.
Give identifier and fulfillment columns more room according to their longer content.
d3.h_vs_v: A wider table preserves identifiers and short rows but requires horizontal scrolling. Fitting the viewport avoids scrolling at the cost of broken identifiers, taller rows, and slower comparison.

analysis.strengths: All columns are visible at once, headers stay on one line, and each data row is limited to two lines. The SKU and warehouse values break at hyphens, preserving useful segments.
analysis.faults: The two tracking numbers break inside their uninterrupted identifiers, making them harder to read and copy. The two-line rows also leave substantial empty space in the short-value columns.
analysis.spatial_logic: Space is concentrated on SKU, warehouse and tracking while the remaining columns are kept close to their content widths. The table uses the full viewport.

analysis.strengths: All columns are visible at once, and the wider tracking column puts more of each tracking number on its first line. Headers remain on one line.
analysis.faults: Tracking numbers still break inside the identifiers, while each SKU occupies four lines. This makes every data row much taller and weakens the connection between each SKU and its other values.
analysis.spatial_logic: Twenty pixels move from SKU to tracking compared with P. The extra tracking width does not prevent identifier breaks, but the lost SKU width triggers a large increase in row height.

analysis.strengths: All columns are visible at once, headers remain on one line, and the data rows stay at two lines. SKU and warehouse values break at hyphens.
analysis.faults: The tracking numbers still break inside their uninterrupted identifiers. Its small width changes relative to P do not produce a visible improvement in row height or the shown breaks.
analysis.spatial_logic: R gives tracking slightly more room than P by narrowing SKU, while keeping the same compact two-line structure and fitting within 719 pixels.

analysis.strengths: Every value stays on one line, including the tracking numbers. Short, uniform rows make comparisons and SKU lookup easy, with no breaks inside words.
analysis.faults: The table requires horizontal scrolling, and the initial viewport shows only the beginning of the tracking column. Tracking lookup therefore requires a scroll, and the row context becomes less immediately available.
analysis.spatial_logic: SKU, warehouse and tracking receive enough width for their longest complete values. The extra width buys intact identifiers and compact rows at the cost of first-sight visibility.

rounds.insights: The decisive widths belong to SKU, warehouse and tracking; the other columns are already close to their content needs. Within 719 pixels, keeping all three comfortable is impossible: P and R preserve a useful two-line rhythm but split tracking identifiers, while Q demonstrates that moving a little more space to tracking can greatly worsen SKU wrapping without solving the tracking break. Scrolling can preserve the tracking numbers, and allowing SKU and warehouse to wrap at hyphens can reduce the scroll distance compared with S.

analysis.strengths: All text is intact, headers remain on one line, and tracking numbers are preserved as single units. SKU and warehouse values wrap at hyphens.
analysis.faults: The initial viewport cuts through the tracking numbers, so they require horizontal scrolling to read. Wrapping SKU and warehouse values makes every data row twice the header height.
analysis.spatial_logic: The compact columns leave enough space for most fields at first sight, while the final 80 px are reached by scrolling.

analysis.strengths: The whole table is visible at once, headers stay on one line, and SKU and warehouse values wrap at hyphens.
analysis.faults: Both tracking numbers break inside their uninterrupted strings, making them harder to read and verify. The stated 720 px width is also 1 px above the 719 px fitting target.
analysis.spatial_logic: Width is taken from SKU and tracking to eliminate scrolling, while the resulting two-line cells determine the height of every data row.

analysis.strengths: The table fits within 719 px, with all headers on one line and SKU and warehouse values wrapping at hyphens.
analysis.faults: Both tracking numbers still break inside their uninterrupted strings. The extra tracking width compared with P does not visibly remove that break, while the narrower SKU column offers no clear reading benefit.
analysis.spatial_logic: This shifts 5 px from SKU toward tracking relative to P; the rendered line pattern and row heights remain essentially the same.

analysis.strengths: Every value remains on one line, making rows compact and identifiers easy to scan and compare. The full table has a clear, even rhythm.
analysis.faults: The initial viewport shows only the beginning of the tracking column, so reading any complete tracking number requires a larger horizontal scroll than in s0B.
analysis.spatial_logic: Wider SKU and warehouse columns remove all wrapping, trading a 142 px overflow for four uniformly short rows.

rounds.insights: The central tradeoff is between seeing every column at once and preserving tracking numbers as whole identifiers. Among scrolling layouts, extra width for both SKU and warehouse produces the compact rows of S, but pushes tracking farther out of the initial view. In the fitting layouts, modest width shifts between SKU and tracking do not eliminate the tracking breaks.

analysis.strengths: All columns and headers are visible at once. The warehouse values wrap at hyphens, and the numeric columns remain easy to scan.
analysis.faults: SKUs occupy four lines, making every data row tall. The tracking numbers break inside uninterrupted identifiers, which makes them harder to read and transcribe.
analysis.spatial_logic: The narrow SKU column drives the height of the whole table, leaving substantial empty space in the shorter cells.

analysis.strengths: Tracking numbers and warehouse values remain whole, while SKUs wrap at hyphens into two lines. The rows are consistent and comparatively compact.
analysis.faults: The first viewport cuts through the Tracking header and values, so tracking lookup requires scrolling. The wide warehouse column buys a single line but adds scroll distance.
analysis.spatial_logic: Width is concentrated on the longer identifiers and locations; their cleaner reading comes at the cost of a wider table.

analysis.strengths: The whole table fits in the viewport, with all headers on one line and data rows limited to two lines. SKU and warehouse wraps occur at useful hyphen boundaries.
analysis.faults: Both tracking numbers break inside the identifier. That is a significant drawback for tracking lookup and transcription.
analysis.spatial_logic: Space is redistributed from SKU and tracking to achieve a compact, fully visible table; the result is balanced in height but compromises the longest unbreakable values.

analysis.strengths: Tracking numbers remain whole, and SKU and warehouse values wrap at hyphens in two-line rows. It requires less scrolling than s1C.
analysis.faults: Tracking values extend beyond the initial viewport. Warehouse values require a second line, and SKUs still wrap despite their relatively wide column.
analysis.spatial_logic: The narrower warehouse column saves 41px without increasing row height, since the SKU column already makes every data row two lines tall.

analysis.strengths: Every value stays on one line, making the table especially easy to scan and compare. The compact, uniform rows give it a clear visual rhythm.
analysis.faults: It is the widest proposal, and the initial viewport shows almost none of the tracking column. Tracking lookup requires the most horizontal travel.
analysis.spatial_logic: The extra width removes all wrapping and reduces row height, trading viewport coverage for continuous identifiers and compact rows.

rounds.insights: The principal tradeoff is between seeing every column at once and keeping tracking numbers intact. R is the strongest fitting layout so far, though its broken tracking identifiers are a real functional cost. S gives the clearest complete-table reading when scrolling is acceptable; s0B offers a narrower scrolling alternative with intact tracking numbers. Once SKU wrapping makes rows two lines tall, wrapping warehouse values can save width without making the table taller.

analysis.strengths: All columns and complete tracking values are visible without scrolling; headers remain on one line.
analysis.faults: The SKU column breaks identifiers into as many as six lines, including breaks within words. The resulting tall rows make scanning and matching records difficult.
analysis.spatial_logic: Protecting tracking and warehouse widths consumes space needed by SKU, leaving most other cells surrounded by excessive vertical whitespace.

analysis.strengths: SKU and warehouse wrap at hyphens, tracking values remain whole, and the three rows have a consistent two-line rhythm. It requires only 59 px of horizontal scrolling.
analysis.faults: SKU identifiers still require two lines, and the first viewport cuts through the tracking values, so their endings require scrolling.
analysis.spatial_logic: Width is concentrated where it prevents internal breaks, while compact numeric columns keep the scroll distance modest.

analysis.strengths: The entire table fits in the viewport, with consistent two-line rows and readable headers. SKU and warehouse wrap at hyphens.
analysis.faults: Tracking identifiers break across lines without a semantic break, making them harder to read and transcribe.
analysis.spatial_logic: It reallocates width from tracking to SKU, producing a much better fit than s2A at the cost of splitting tracking numbers.

analysis.strengths: All values remain intact at the word level, tracking stays on one line, and rows have a consistent height.
analysis.faults: SKU and warehouse still wrap, while the wider SKU column adds 21 px of scrolling relative to s2B without reducing row height. Tracking is more heavily cut off in the first viewport.
analysis.spatial_logic: The extra SKU width shifts its line break but does not change the two-line structure, making it a weak trade for the additional scroll distance.

analysis.strengths: Every value is on one line, making identifiers easy to read and rows easy to compare. The table is compact vertically and visually orderly.
analysis.faults: The first viewport shows only the beginning of tracking, and reaching its full values requires 142 px of scrolling.
analysis.spatial_logic: Generous SKU and warehouse widths eliminate wrapping but push nearly the whole tracking column beyond the initial view.

rounds.insights: The central trade-off is between preserving complete identifiers and keeping tracking visible at first sight. R is the strongest fit-to-viewport layout, although it splits tracking numbers. Among scrolling layouts, s2B minimizes scrolling while preserving unbreakable units; S favors rapid one-line record scanning at the cost of a substantially larger scroll. s0B adds width without improving the row structure.

bad.why: The narrow SKU column fragments identifiers across up to six lines, including breaks inside tokens, making lookup difficult and producing excessively tall rows.
SKUs occupy four lines while tracking numbers still break inside unbroken identifiers. The added height brings little benefit over Layout R.

contrast.why: Equal widths give short fields unnecessary space while forcing SKUs, warehouse names and tracking numbers into narrow columns. Identifiers would wrap heavily or break inside tokens.

sameFunctionGroups.why: These fields identify records, products, locations or shipments, but their contents have very different lengths. Each needs enough width for its own identifiers.
Color and size are product attributes, but their labels and values differ in width; equal columns would not improve comparison.
Price, tax and total are monetary fields and benefit from consistent numeric alignment, but their headings and values do not require identical widths.

synthesis.rationale: Layout S keeps every value on one line, making product and shipment identifiers easiest to scan and copy, at the cost of horizontal scrolling. Layout R is the strongest fitting candidate: its compact rows and hyphen-based SKU and warehouse wraps preserve useful structure, though both tracking numbers break within an unbroken identifier. Layout P has a similar compromise, while s2B and s1C preserve tracking numbers but still wrap other identifiers and require scrolling.

general: Protect the integrity of identifiers and other values readers may need to recognize, compare or copy.
Allocate width according to content and reading task; related columns can use different widths while retaining consistent alignment.
Judge a scrolling table both as a complete table and in its initial viewport.
specific: The tracking values need 180 px including padding and border to remain on one line.
Layout S needs 142 px of horizontal scrolling but keeps all three data rows on one line.
Among the fitting candidates, Layout R preserves two-line rows while accepting breaks in the two tracking values.

synthesis.tradeoffs: Layout S favors continuous identifiers and compact rows; its tracking column is mostly outside the initial viewport. Layout R exposes all columns at once but splits tracking numbers, so it is a conditional fitting finalist rather than an equally strong choice for tracking lookup.
synthesis.uncertain: The preferred class depends on how often readers need tracking numbers and whether horizontal scrolling is obvious in the actual interface. The renders do not establish how copied wrapped identifiers behave.

critique.cause: The 100px SKU and 102px warehouse columns force wrapping; the 180px tracking column puts the table 44px beyond the viewport.

critique.good: The entire table fits, headers and short fields stay whole, and two-line rows are more compact than in d3r2A.
critique.problems: Tracking identifiers split inside the value. SKU and warehouse wrapping also slows line identification, though their breaks follow hyphens.
critique.cause: Tracking has only 136px, while SKU and warehouse have 100px and 102px respectively.

critique.good: Every value stays on one line, making rows compact and supporting rapid comparison and lookup. Widths follow the content and the full table has a clear, even rhythm.
critique.problems: The initial viewport shows only the start of the tracking column; reading or copying a tracking identifier requires scrolling. The full table is substantially wider than the viewport.
critique.cause: The 157px SKU, 143px warehouse and 180px tracking columns preserve complete values but produce a table 142px wider than the viewport.

d2r1A.idea: Scrolling alternative: keep SKU and tracking whole, but wrap warehouse values at hyphens. This tests whether moving Tracking 41 px closer to the initial viewport is worth taller rows.

d2r1B.idea: Viewport-fitting alternative totaling 719 px: give Tracking more room than in A while preserving whole headers and numeric fields. SKU and warehouse can wrap at hyphens; tracking must still split, so inspect the resulting breaks and row heights.

d3r1A.idea: Test a 719 px fitting layout. Preserve whole short headers, colors, sizes, quantities, and amounts; allow SKU and warehouse to wrap at hyphens and give the remaining width to tracking. Tracking must split, but the table requires no horizontal scrolling.

d3r1B.idea: Test a scrolling compromise with whole warehouse and tracking identifiers. SKU wraps at hyphens, saving 57 px compared with d3r0C and bringing more of Tracking into the initial viewport.

d1r1A.idea: Test a 719px viewport-fitting layout. Preserve the Warehouse header and give SKU enough room for more useful hyphen breaks, accepting that tracking identifiers must split within their text.

d1r1B.idea: Test a 799px scrolling compromise: keep warehouse codes and tracking identifiers on one line while allowing SKUs to wrap at hyphens. This tests whether whole fulfillment details justify 40px more scrolling than d1r0B.

d2r2A.idea: Test a viewport-fitting alternative that gives SKU enough width for more meaningful two-line breaks. Reduce tracking width to pay for it; tracking will still split, but the shorter SKU rows may substantially improve the table's density and scanning.

d1r2A.idea: Fit within 719 px while giving SKU enough room for two-line hyphenated breaks. Warehouse also wraps at hyphens; tracking must break within its identifiers, but the table may gain shorter, more consistent rows than d1r1A.

d1r2B.idea: Keep SKU and tracking identifiers whole while allowing warehouse codes to wrap at hyphens. This reduces scrolling relative to d1r0C while preserving the product and shipment identifiers on one line.

d3r2A.idea: Try a fitting layout that gives tracking 15px more by narrowing SKU. This may make tracking endings easier to read, at the cost of potentially less natural SKU wrapping.

d3r2B.idea: Try a compact scrolling layout with intact tracking values and minimum-width warehouse text. SKU already determines row height, so warehouse wrapping may reduce scrolling without making rows taller.

d3r3A.idea: Do not render: this repeats d3r1A; retained here only as a reference.

d3r3B.idea: Keep warehouse and tracking identifiers whole while allowing SKU to wrap at hyphens. This tests whether a modest scroll reduction from d3r0C is worthwhile when warehouse lookup remains uninterrupted.

d1r3A.idea: Test a compact scrolling layout: wrap SKU and warehouse codes at hyphens while keeping tracking identifiers whole. It should reduce the scrolling distance and expose more of Tracking initially.

d1r3B.idea: Test a middle ground that wraps SKU but keeps warehouse and tracking values whole. This moves fulfillment information left compared with d1r0C while preserving continuous warehouse codes.

s0A.idea: A compact scrolling compromise: retain R's two-line SKU and warehouse treatment, but give tracking its full 180 pixels so its identifiers remain whole. At 759 pixels wide, it should require substantially less scrolling than S while preserving natural breaks.

s0B.idea: A roomier scrolling alternative that gives SKU more space while keeping tracking identifiers whole and allowing warehouse values to wrap at hyphens. At 800 pixels wide, it should expose more of tracking initially than S; actual SKU wrapping should be checked in the render.

s1A.idea: Test a fitting layout that gives tracking 20 px more than R by narrowing SKU. Check whether longer tracking fragments improve verification and whether SKU wrapping remains acceptable.

s1B.idea: Keep SKU and tracking on one line while allowing warehouse values to wrap. This tests a middle ground between s0B and S, with 101 px of overflow.

s1C.idea: Keep warehouse and tracking on one line while allowing SKU values to wrap. Compare its lookup rhythm and 121 px of overflow with the other scrolling options.

s2A.idea: Test a fitting layout that preserves whole tracking numbers by taking 40px from R's SKU column. This deliberately prioritizes tracking identifiers; inspect whether the resulting SKU breaks and taller rows are acceptable.

s2B.idea: Reduce s0B's SKU column by 21px to shorten the scroll distance while retaining whole tracking numbers. Check whether SKUs still wrap cleanly at hyphens within two lines.

s3A.idea: Keep R's compact SKU and two-line rows, but restore the full tracking width. At 759 px, it may preserve all unbreakable units with only 39 px of scrolling; verify SKU wrapping in the render.

s3B.idea: Keep SKU and tracking on one line while allowing warehouse names to wrap at hyphens. At 821 px, this tests whether easier SKU lookup justifies 62 px more scrolling than the compact refinement.

contrast.idea: Equal widths give short fields unnecessary space while forcing SKUs, warehouse names and tracking numbers into narrow columns. Identifiers would wrap heavily or break inside tokens.
